item.title: El Niño May Cause Fewer Hurricanes in North America, Limiting Insurance Losses, Zurich CEO Says
item.description: The development of El Niño climate phenomenon might limit catastrophe claims in North America, the CEO of Zurich Insurance said last week after it reported second-quarter results. “What we hear is that this development of El Niño is actually moderating the risk of typhoons and hurricanes, especially on the American coasts. coastlines have increased the amount of property exposed to hurricanes, meaning that even a relatively quiet hurricane season can produce severe losses.

item.title: Alacrity Solutions Names Triola Chief Revenue Officer
item.description: Alacrity Solutions Group LLC named Tony Triola chief revenue officer. Triola will oversee Alacrity’s revenue strategy, including business development, sales and customer growth initiatives. Alacrity is a provider of insurance claims management services, delivering property, auto, and casualty claims adjustment, staffing support, temporary housing services, in addition to subrogation and recovery solutions.

item.title: Allstate Introduces Large Language Model, ALLIE
item.description: Allstate CEO Tom Wilson said the insurer has a “technology-drive strategy, not a strategy supported by technology.” And the next step in the strategy is the build of ALLIE – Allstate’s Large Language Intelligent Ecosystem. The coordination and configuration of the computer systems it has already built “is helping us accelerate the build and deployment of ALLIE.” Wilson told the analysts that the large language model is “just another step along the continuum that we’ve been on for a long time” when it comes to artificial intelligence. He said Allstate spends a “tremendous amount of time and effort on cybersecurity,” adding he is “concerned about the large language models that now break out on their own and tell other agents how to do it without getting caught.”

item.title: DAC Beachcroft expands Cyber team with three new partners
item.description: International law firm DAC Beachcroft has bolstered its Cyber and Data Risk practice with the appointment of three specialist cyber partners: Richard Breavington, Rachel Ford, and Daniel Guilfoyle. The trio joins from RPC where they were partners in its Cyber & Technology Insurance team, led by Breavington. All three partners bring extensive experience of advising insurers and corporates across a range of industry sectors on high value and multi-jurisdictional cyber incidents, data breaches as well as technology errors & omissions claims.

item.title: REVO submits binding offer to acquire Eurocaution in planned Benelux expansion
item.description: REVO Insurance S.p.A., an Italian speciality non-life insurer, has announced the submission of a binding offer to acquire Luxembourg-based Eurocaution S.A. According to REVO Insurance, the acquisition would represent another step in its international expansion strategy following the launch of its Spanish operations in November 2024. The insurer stated that adding Eurocaution to the group would strengthen its presence in the European surety market, an area where REVO Insurance already holds a leading position in Italy.

item.title: Accredited selects Hellenic Hull as first dedicated ocean marine MGA partner
item.description: The agreement establishes Hellenic Hull as Accredited’s first dedicated MGA partner for these classes and marks the insurer’s strategic expansion into specialist ocean marine underwriting. We look forward to working with Ilias and his team to develop a profitable and sustainable marine portfolio together.” Ilias Tsakiris, Chief Executive Officer of Hellenic Hull, said, “We are very pleased to welcome Accredited as a new partner and particularly proud that Hellenic Hull has been selected for its first dedicated ocean marine programme. Hellenic Hull’s depth of marine expertise, established distribution, integrated claims capabilities and disciplined underwriting approach made it the right partner for our first dedicated Hull & Machinery and Marine Cargo program.

item.title: Taylor Farms Recalls Salsa and Guacamole Over Salmonella Risk
item.description: Taylor Farms on Sunday said it was recalling more than a dozen prepared food items containing jalapeños, including salsas and guacamole, from retailers over concerns about potential salmonella contamination. Taylor Farms is unaware of any reported illnesses linked to the voluntarily recalled items the statement added. health authorities investigate a Salmonella outbreak linked to jalapeño peppers imported from Mexico that earlier this week had sickened 345 people across 27 states and led to 36 hospitalizations.

item.title: Heat Deaths Top 25,000 in Europe as Scorching Weather Persists
item.description: Extreme heat has killed more than 25,000 people across Europe this year, according to the latest available data compiled by Bloomberg. Germany recorded the highest toll, with an estimated 11,900 excess deaths linked to heat since April, according to the Robert Koch Institute . Western Europe has been seared by four heat waves this summer, shattering temperature records and denting economic output.

item.title: OpenAI Pauses Some Work on New Astra Model on Cyber Concerns
item.description: OpenAI said it’s now taking steps to improve security controls for developing and testing newer models and “pausing internal activities involving Astra that do not yet meet these strengthened security control requirements.” Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman said the company is working to make the model “generally available.” “Given its cyber capabilities, we need a little longer to do this safely,” Altman said Friday in a social media post . OpenAI is pausing some internal work around one of its upcoming artificial intelligence models to implement stricter safeguards after the system was found to be significantly more adept at cybersecurity tasks. The ChatGPT maker said on Friday it “cannot rule out” that the unreleased Astra model would reach OpenAI’s “critical cybersecurity threshold,” meaning it’s capable of identifying and developing zero-day exploits without human intervention.

item.title: As Wildfires Destroy and Displace, APCIA Says Congress Must Pass Fix Our Forests Act
item.description: “The devastating wildfires unfolding across the country underscore the urgent need for Congress to pass the bipartisan Fix Our Forests Act,” said David A. In the meantime, sitting in Congress is a piece of federal legislation lawmakers in the House and Senate propped up following the destructive, headline-grabbing Los Angeles wildfires to start 2025. Wildfires have again become a major headline as about 10% of the population of Spokane, Washington has been ordered to leave their homes, and hundreds of structures have been destroyed.

item.title: Higginbotham opens El Paso office
item.description: Higginbotham has opened an office in El Paso, Texas, expanding its physical footprint in a market where it has served clients for years. The office will be led by Micah Harrison, vice president of employee benefits, who joined Higginbotham in 2025 and has more than two decades of industry experience. The El Paso opening is part of Higginbotham’s broader expansion strategy.

item.title: Franklin Madison names chief growth & strategy officer
item.description: Franklin Madison announced the appointment of Matt Bishop as chief growth and strategy officer. In the newly created role, Bishop will lead Franklin Madison’s enterprise growth strategy, long-term planning and innovation initiatives. Franklin Madison partners with more than 3,500 financial institutions to distribute insurance products and marketing services.

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway P&C reinsurance boosted by Tokio Marine deal, as property volumes fall
item.description: While Berkshire Hathaway has reported declining premium volumes in property business across both its primary insurance and reinsurance businesses, likely due to the softening of pricing we assume, its P&C reinsurance arm was boosted by the recent agreement and whole account deal with Tokio Marine. Berkshire Hathaway, the American multinational conglomerate holding company, reported that its recently entered into whole account quota share reinsurance agreement with Tokio Marine boosted premium volumes in the second-quarter, which otherwise would have fallen primarily due to lower property underwriting volumes. Recall that, back in the first-quarter of this year, Berkshire Hathaway’s reinsurance arm National Indemnity Company (NICO) acquired a 2.5% stake in the Japanese insurer, in a deal that comprised the following three key elements: strategic equity investment in Tokio Marine Holdings, Inc., collaboration in reinsurance, and strategic collaboration in M&A and global investment opportunities.

item.title: Gradient AI refreshes brand as business scales
item.description: Gradient AI has introduced a new brand identity as the insurance AI company looks to reflect its expansion beyond its startup roots. Founded in 2018, Gradient AI provides AI-powered decision intelligence to carriers, TPAs, brokers, self-insured employers, MGAs and other insurance organizations across group health, P&C and workers’ compensation. The company said it has experienced double-digit year-over-year growth and has built a data lake spanning tens of millions of policies and claims.

item.title: Intact launches $1 million Olympian community grant program
item.description: Intact Insurance and the Canadian Olympic Committee (COC) have launched Intact Olympian Impact, a three-year, C$1 million program that will fund community sports initiatives led by Team Canada Olympians. The initiative builds on the former OLY Canada Legacy Grant program and has previously supported projects including Charles Hamelin’s Glissez vers l’Integration , Laura Stacey’s S7 Sticks In For Charity Road Hockey Tournament , and Oluseyi Smith’s Racing to Zero . The program will award grants to Canadian Olympians to support projects focused on expanding access to sport, promoting healthy play for youth, and advancing sustainability, in line with the COC’s Team Canada 2035 strategy centered on Play, Podium, and Planet.

item.title: Inszone acquires Washington employee benefits agency Radwick & Lightle
item.description: Inszone Insurance has acquired The Lightle Group, LLC, doing business as Radwick & Lightle, expanding its employee benefits operations in Washington. The acquisition brings Radwick & Lightle’s employee benefits team into Inszone, providing access to a broader range of insurance markets, technology, and operational resources while maintaining the agency’s existing client service model. Founded in 2001 by Curt Lightle and based in Bremerton, Washington, Radwick & Lightle specializes in employee benefits for small and midsize businesses, offering benefits consulting, HR support, compliance services, and claims advocacy.

item.title: Open finance en Perú pone a prueba los límites regulatorios sobre los datos
item.description: La falta de claridad sobre la gestión de las entidades reguladoras en la gestión del consentimiento e intercambio de datos es lo que más preocupa a la industria sobre el próximo Sistema de Finanzas Abiertas (SFA) de Perú. La Superintendencia de Bancos, Seguros y AFP (SBS) ha declarado que mantiene coordinación con la Autoridad Nacional de Protección de Datos Personales (ANPDP) y otras autoridades, pero los bancos aún tienen dudas sobre cómo será la vigilancia y aplicación de sanciones en los acuerdos de datos compartidos. “No queda claro si la Autoridad Nacional de Protección de Datos tiene algún tipo de voz y voto en esto”, dijo a iupana un experto legal de un banco local.

item.title: Finsus cambia modelo de riesgo para prestar a conductores de plataformas
item.description: La garantía de un vehículo cambió la forma en que Finsus evalúa a los trabajadores de plataformas de transporte, pues la empresa asegura que ese respaldo le permitió adaptar sus modelos de riesgo y ofrecer crédito a un segmento que, sin esa estructura, seguiría siendo mucho más difícil de financiar. Los trabajadores de plataformas digitales han sido un segmento difícil de atender para la banca por la variabilidad de sus ingresos y la ausencia de esquemas laborales tradicionales. En América Latina y el Caribe, el 52% de estos trabajadores utiliza estas aplicaciones como una fuente complementaria de ingresos, según la OIT.

item.title: Buenas Fuentes: Nequi se independiza y Hey Banco amplía pagos
item.description: Hey Banco de México amplía pagos con tapi Hey Banco integró la infraestructura de tapi para habilitar el pago de servicios desde su aplicación, como parte de su estrategia para consolidar un ecosistema financiero todo en uno. Nequi operará como Compañía de Financiamiento en Colombia Nequi comenzará a operar como Compañía de Financiamiento desde el 1 de septiembre, convirtiéndose en una entidad independiente dentro del Grupo Cibest en Colombia. La alianza también contempla incorporar recargas y pagos programados en futuras etapas.

item.title: ClaimsBridge Adds Capital, Acquires DialysisPPO
item.description: (Image source: ClaimsBridge website.) ClaimsBridge (Arnold, Md.) has received a strategic investment from Eir Partners Capital (Miami) and acquired DialysisPPO (King of Prussia, Pa.), a cost-containment company focused on end-stage renal disease and chronic dialysis treatment. ClaimsBridge says Eir’s investment will provide capital and operational support while leaving its existing client team, processes and service model in place. “Eir’s investment gives us the ability to accelerate innovation for our clients and the payer market, and DialysisPPO is the strongest solution we’ve seen for one of healthcare’s most complex and expensive conditions.” Founded in 2006, DialysisPPO provides a patented program that allows health plans to capture Medicare savings on dialysis claims immediately, rather than waiting for the typical 30-month coordination period, according to ClaimsBridge.

item.title: Federated Acquires HDVI
item.description: (Image credit: Zetong Li/Unsplash.) High Definition Vehicle Insurance (HDVI; Greenville, S.C.) has been acquired by Federated Mutual Insurance Company (Owatonna, Minn.). HDVI will operate as a largely autonomous subsidiary of Federated Insurance, retaining its separate operations, employees and agency relationships. “Our success and progress attracted the attention of major organizations across the nation, and we are very pleased to have found a home with the established, value-driven, and well-capitalized Federated Insurance,” comments Adam Barnett, President and CEO, HDVI.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $567 Million In New Mexico for Teen Mental Health Fund
item.description: A New Mexico state court ordered Meta on Thursday to pay $567 million into a teen mental health fund and change how its platforms function for young users after finding the company is to blame for harming children’s wellbeing. The ruling comes five months after a New Mexico jury in an earlier phase of the case ordered Meta to pay $375 million after finding it violated consumer protection law by misrepresenting the safety of Facebook and Instagram for young users. Biedscheid on Thursday ordered Meta to implement youth-safety measures, including monthly limits on teens’ use of Facebook and Instagram, restrictions on notifications, tighter controls on adult contact with minors, safeguards for AI chatbots, and enhanced review of child sexual abuse reports, under a decree that will be in place for five years.

item.title: Arson Suspect Timed Spokane Fire for High Wind Day
item.description: The 37-year old man suspected of starting one of the fires burning around Spokane, Washington told a detective that he planned the arson attack for Sunday to coincide with a “high winds” day, according to court documents. Red-flag fire warnings have been posted across parts of Oregon and Washington, including Spokane, where a dry weather front is expected to bring wind gusts up to 30 miles (48 kilometers) per hour, according to the National Weather Service. Related: Washington Man Charged With Starting Devastating Spokane Fire Sunday’s blaze was one of 16 other large fires burning this week in Washington state.

item.title: Swiss Re Profit Beats Estimates as Reinsurer Boosts Cost Cuts
item.description: Swiss Re AG’s first-half profit beat estimates as the reinsurer saw all key business units perform in line with targets, while the firm announced a fresh round of cost cuts. Swiss Re announced that it is raising its operating-cost reduction target to $500 million by 2028, up from a prior goal of $300 million by 2027. Profit for the second quarter was $1.3 billion, resulting in net income of $2.8 billion for the six months to June, the Zurich-based company said in a statement Thursday.

item.title: ILS and alt capital remains disciplined amid record cat bond market growth: J.P. Morgan
item.description: Morgan has suggested that while the catastrophe bond market has witnessed exceptional growth in 2026, insurance-linked securities (ILS) and alternative capital are looking more disciplined, exhibiting few of the undisciplined behaviours witnessed in the last soft market. Q2 2026 also featured the largest month of cat bond issuance since Artemis began tracking the sector, as the record 20 deals completed in May brought almost $7 billion of risk capital to market. As highlighted in Artemis’ Q2 2026 Cat Bond & ILS market report , the second quarter of 2026 marked the largest ever quarter recorded for cat bond issuance, as it became the first-time quarterly issuance surpassed $11 billion, beating the previous record set in H1 2025 by over $842 million.

item.title: Twelve Securis combining cat bond and private ILS management teams, as Schwartz to depart
item.description: Twelve Securis is combining its catastrophe bond and private ILS focused investment teams, to consolidate and optimise its approach to managing dedicated strategies and blended portfolios, while at the same time the firm also stated that long-standing senior employee Etienne Schwartz is departing the firm. Twelve Securis, the specialist catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities (ILS) investment manager, is bringing responsibilities for analytics, portfolio and investment management of both cat bonds and private ILS together now, seeing this as a more efficient approach. Twelve Securis stated that in bringing together its catastrophe bond and private ILS portfolio, analytics and investment teams, it is aiming to achieve more efficient portfolio construction.

item.title: Amwins Global Risks broadens global renewable energy catastrophe facility and raises capacity to $50m
item.description: Amwins Global Risks, the specialist wholesale insurance broking business of Amwins, has expanded its specialist natural catastrophe facility for renewable energy projects, increasing available capacity to USD $50 million per placement while extending both the range of covered perils and its global availability. Harry Downes, Director at Amwins Global Risks, commented: “Renewable energy projects are becoming larger, more valuable and increasingly exposed to a broader range of natural catastrophe risks. This facility helps clients close that gap and build greater resilience into their insurance programmes.” Amwins Global Risks added that the enhanced facility is part of its ongoing investment in specialist insurance solutions for the global renewable energy market and is available through the company’s Energy, Power & Infrastructure practice.

item.title: Octave Specialty grows Q2’26 revenue 51% as underwriting performance improves
item.description: Octave Specialty Group, a US-listed global specialty insurance company operating across insurance distribution and specialty property and casualty insurance, reported improved second-quarter 2026 results, supported by stronger underwriting performance at its Everspan insurance business and continued expansion across its insurance distribution operations. Octave Specialty Group attributed the increase primarily to its Insurance Distribution segment, reflecting the acquisition of ArmadaCare alongside organic revenue growth of 44%. Claude LeBlanc, President and Chief Executive Officer of Octave, commented: “Our core Insurance Distribution business delivered another quarter of strong performance led by revenue growth of 77% and organic revenue growth of 44%.

item.title: ALIRT reveals contrasting residual property insurance trends across four high-risk US states
item.description: In its latest biannual publication, Residual Property Market Trends in Four Higher Risk States, ALIRT points to a significant improvement in underwriting results across US property insurance during 2025.The homeowners insurance segment generated approximately $17 billion in underwriting profit, marking its strongest annual performance in more than ten years. ALIRT Insurance Research, a US insurance research and analytics firm focused on the property and casualty sector, has released a new report highlighting widening differences in the performance of residual property insurance markets across California, Florida, Louisiana, and Texas. The company says that although the wider US property insurance market has returned to profitability, conditions within higher-risk states continue to follow very different paths.

item.title: Pritzker Signs Bills Giving Insurance Department Power to Overturn Rate Changes
item.description: Pritzker and Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias have pushed lawmakers for years to give the insurance department more authority to reel in rate increases. Pritzker this week signed legislation that gives the state’s insurance department authority to object rates it deems are excessive, inadequate, or unfairly discriminatory. “This law puts consumers first by giving Illinois the authority to challenge excessive rate hikes – increasing transparency in the insurance marketplace and ensuring drivers are no longer left paying the price,” Giannoulias said.

item.title: Texas Bakery Fined $25K for Child Labor and Back Wages Violations
item.description: Department of Labor has recovered thousands in back wages and assessed penalties after a federal investigation revealed child labor, minimum wage, and overtime violations by the operators of three La Panaderia Bakery & Café locations in San Antonio. The division assessed a $25,706 civil money penalty for the child labor violations. Division investigators found the employers violated child labor provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act.

item.description: The move was in contrast to the Republican’s typical pro-business stature, underlining how the data center debate has put Texas conservatives between Trump and angry constituents in rural, unincorporated areas where The Texas Tribune has reported most planned data centers are set to be located. President Donald Trump this week criticized Texas for being anti-data centers, just days after Republican Gov. “I saw Texas the other day sort of is against data centers,” Trump said in a nearly hourlong sit-down interview with Punchbowl News released Friday.

item.title: AXA XL to acquire remaining stake in cyber security consultancy S-RM
item.description: AXA XL has agreed to acquire the remaining shares of London-based corporate intelligence and cyber security consultancy S-RM , expanding its risk prevention capabilities beyond traditional insurance coverage. Founded in 2005, S-RM provides corporate intelligence, cyber security and crisis response services to businesses and investors globally. AXA XL currently owns approximately 49% of S-RM and will acquire the outstanding shares under an agreement subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Q2 profit rises 43% on underwriting improvement and investment gains
item.description: The post Liberty Mutual Q2 profit rises 43% on underwriting improvement and investment gains appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Liberty Mutual reported second-quarter 2026 net income of $2.63 billion , up 43% from the prior-year period, as improved underwriting results, lower catastrophe losses and stronger investment performance supported earnings. For the first half of 2026, Liberty Mutual reported net income attributable to the company of  $4.69 billion , representing a 63% increase compared with the same period in 2025.

item.title: Jewelers Mutual backs jewelry software platform Luxe
item.description: Jewelers Mutual has made a strategic investment in Luxe Software , a vertical software and payments platform for independent jewelry retailers, alongside venture capital firm K5 Global. Founded in New York, Luxe provides an all-in-one platform that combines point-of-sale, CRM, payments, two-way texting, business phone, and reporting tools designed specifically for independent jewelers. For Jewelers Mutual, the investment aligns with its broader strategy of supporting technology providers serving the jewelry industry.

item.title: Trupanion: Pets Best is winding down, Chewy remains small
item.description: Chewy remains a small contributor Trupanion didn’t mention Chewy on the earnings call, but the comparison is worth noting. Here are the key takeaways from the earnings call: Trupanion is moving on from Pets Best The company said it has agreed with Pets Best to conclude their relationship following the third quarter of 2028, a move that makes strategic sense after JAB indirectly acquired Pets Best in 2024. “Every dollar we invest in pet acquisition today has the potential to create significantly more long-term value than it did just a year ago.” New products remain on track Management said its new digital insurance offering remains on schedule to launch by the midpoint of its current strategic plan, targeting customer segments not currently served by Trupanion’s flagship product.
